summary: A 1970 response by Steve Crocker to RFC 67, which proposed changing the host-IMP specification. It is part of the discussion.

eli5.summary: A reply to a suggestion, giving the author's view.

subtitle: An early 1970 response cautioning against premature protocol changes.

tldr.problem: There were suggestions to modify the early network protocol, but early implementers disagreed about whether to adopt them.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC author argues for prioritizing implementation and field experience before making non-critical changes, polling sites to validate this policy.
tldr.outcome: The focus remained on implementing the existing protocol first and gathering real-world experience before designing improvements.

today: RFC 73 is an Internet Experiment document. It captures policy guidance from the early ARPA network and remains historically significant as an example of engineering pragmatism in protocol design.

sections.title: Response to Protocol Change Suggestions
sections.content:
RFC 73 is a brief response by Steve Crocker addressing a proposal in RFC 67 to modify the host-IMP specification. The author acknowledges that the suggestion is reasonable but argues against adopting it at that time.

The policy prioritized rapid implementation of the existing protocol over premature modifications. Crocker had polled several network sites and found that those actively implementing the network control program (NCP) agreed with this cautious approach, while sites with less implementation progress wanted the suggested change.
sections.eli5: Someone wanted to change how the network worked, but the author polled the other groups and found that the ones building systems wanted to build with what they had first.

sections.title: Learning from Experience
sections.content:
The author makes the case that while improvements are necessary in the long term, clearer ideas about what needs to change will emerge from actual use of the network. Making changes now without field experience risks introducing problems or solving the wrong problems.

The RFC reflects the early experimental nature of the network: the focus was on building working implementations first, documenting lessons learned, and then making informed decisions about protocol improvements.
sections.eli5: You learn what needs fixing by actually using something, not by guessing before you build it.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content: This brief document captures an important moment in network design: the decision to stabilize an experimental protocol and gain operational experience before continuing major changes. This approach influenced how the early ARPA network evolved through multiple iterations as understanding improved.
sections.eli5: The early builders learned that it was smarter to get something working first and then improve it, rather than redesign everything before anyone tried it.
